c74object.name: evi.hardclip~
c74object.description:
evi.hardclip~ is a 'max define' for the evi_hardclip.gendsp gen~ abstraction. Because evi.hardclip~ is a 'max define' it also accepts all messages and attributes that a gen~ object does.
To be used whenever clamping of audio is required, evi.hardclip~ should do a good job of protecting your precious audio. This is because this is antialiased hard clipping capable of high input gain whilst maintaining audio quality. evi.hardclip~ is the hard clipping section from the evi.clip~ object but with more antiderivative and oversampling options for when managing audio quality against CPU usage, selected via the @aa attribute. Increasing @aa does not necessarily translate to 'better'. Experiment with this setting depending on your audio input material.

inlet.digest: Inlet #1: Audio Input to be treated nicely

attribute.name: aa
attribute.description: 'aa' stands for 'Anti-Aliasing'. Select type (or 'strength') here. 0=1st order antiderivative, 1=1st order 2x oversampled, 2=1st order 4x oversampled, 3=2nd order antiderivative (default), 4=2nd order 2x oversampled, 5=2nd order 4x oversampled.

c74object.discussion: This object is for all those MSP users who use [clip~ -1. 1.] at the end of their audio chains. You should never do this - it destroys your audio and aliases like hell. Use evi.hardclip~ instead. It can anti-alias very large gain inputs whilst retaining the clipping functionality you seek.
